scope: Read-only decomposition of already-paid Task B pairs; no new requests or prompt edits.

byteDefinition.opencodeAndKimi: UTF8 compact JSON ensure_ascii=false of message arrays/tools. System/developer separated. Prior history is non-system messages strictly before unique user message containing exact round business prompt. Delivery is non-system messages from that anchor to end of first request, including any native reminders. Business bytes are exact common task prompt UTF8. Arrays include JSON delimiters. No token estimates.
byteDefinition.pi: UTF-8 compact JSON ensure_ascii=False sort_keys=True separators=(comma,colon); text bytes separately. Bytes are not tokens. History includes earlier user/model/tool content; differences are descriptive, not isolated causal effects.

piFixedSystemOrigin.classification: Product generated standing instructions account for 6870 bytes net of common role instruction. Remaining 109 bytes are longer harness-selected channel cwd rendered by Pi. No append accumulation across 12 rounds; serialized once per request. Byte counts are not token estimates.

sharedStandingOrigin.scope: Read-only frozen-source/request attribution; no new requests or cost estimation

opencode.observed: B first request current system includes Instructions from: rah-standing-<digest>.md followed by product Room-first workplace text. Do not equate all 7221 with a pure compiler string.

pi.mechanism: [Loom standing instructions] + nativeFinalTextInstructions(o.prompt,...), passed with --append-system-prompt at line166. Same product compiler origin, different wrapper/native system layout.

kimi.observed: B R1 net system +62 compact UTF8 bytes; principal initial extra instructions are in user delivery (+6939), not system. Later that initial material resides in history. Both B pairs show same byte differences.
kimi.schemaLimitation: ReadMediaFile print/ACP dynamic registration difference remains. No strict schema parity claim.

productAccountingLimitation.reason: Current A arms include native compaction; Kernel retains parse_error gaps. Independently matched summary aggregates do not prove all HTTP consumption. External benchmark totals include all captured raw responses, including summary/retry costs, once.
productAccountingLimitation.auditHelperWarning: aggregateCoverage.productAllConsumptionComplete is always false by design; arm-level completeness comes from current/coverage.mjs, not that helper field.

conclusions: Extra standing content is retained in context; it is not accumulated as a fresh duplicate each turn.
Business prompts match, but sampled output/tool paths create different future histories; preserve paired repeats and per-task results.
Pi B request counts are equal while input differs; request count alone cannot explain overhead. OpenCode B has fewer requests and lower summed input despite larger first requests.
Shared standing/delivery content is a concrete cross-CLI optimization candidate; this observation does not prove shortening it will reduce complete-task cost.
limits: Bytes are not tokens; no estimated token or monetary allocation.
Kimi initial extra content is mainly in user delivery, not system; later it is part of history. Its dynamic tool-schema difference remains.
The two repeats per task do not isolate causal effects or establish statistical equivalence.

priorCandidate.decision: This batch does not reverse the prior decision to stop small prompt-trimming as the main cost work. A standing payload observation is not a new demonstrated optimization.
